accuracy.evidence: Matches Development Matters (3 and 4 year olds, PSED: 'Be increasingly independent in meeting their own care needs, e.g. washing and drying their hands' and birth to three 'Express preferences and decisions'), and the ELOF Self-Awareness goal of describing own preferences. The jobs split follows standard child safety advice: hot ovens, roads and medicine need an adult; coats, handwashing and tidying are age-appropriate self-care.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the documented errors at this age: thinking a friend is wrong for liking something different (challenge 'Only Mia'/'Pip is wrong'), copying a friend's answer instead of stating one's own ('I like cars'), attempting unsafe jobs alone (road, oven, climbing) and the opposite, giving up instead of asking for help ('Give up'). The adult text names all of these.

lab_distinct.evidence: Five different mechanics: a no-wrong-answer preference sort, a choose-three toy grid that reveals a friend's overlapping and different picks, a one-card-at-a-time safety sort with reasons, a hold-to-pour jug with a fill line and real spill, and a three-slot sentence card that builds 'I like... but Pip likes...'. It passed the 30% shingle gate and shares no mechanic with flagfam or flagmood.

lab_teaches.evidence: The child first states likes with any answer accepted, then sees that a friend shares one and differs on two, then learns the line between can-do-alone and ask-a-grown-up with a reason for each, then practises a real independent skill (pouring to a line, stopping before a spill), then uses the curriculum sentence frame on a card made from their own earlier choices.

predictions.evidence: Three locked predictions with a tempting wrong option that the lab then settles: 'Will Pip like all the same toys? Yes, all the same' (Pip shares one and differs on two), 'Crossing the road: I go on my own' (the road job is rejected with the reason), and 'Past the line it stops by itself' (the cup spills).

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six rotating questions with twelve distinct wrong-answer m= messages, each naming the slip: likes are not right or wrong (two versions), road and oven safety, Pip is not wrong, copying Pip's like, pouring past the line, shaking the cup, climbing the shelf, giving up instead of asking, and mixing up I am and I can with I like.

readability.evidence: Kid text is short read-aloud sentences with everyday words (apples, coat, oven, fast cars) within the family FK limit; adult text is within 10.0. Canvas prompts are under eight words, buttons pair one emoji with one or two words, and the young class gives large tap targets.

no_filler.evidence: Passed the filler regex and 12% duplication gate. Each kid paragraph does one job (say a like, compare with a friend, self-care jobs, safety jobs); the adult text covers the skill, the sentence frame, named mistakes and the lab; the family tip is one snack-time game and one real daily job.

mobile.evidence: On the iPhone 13 walkthrough and 360 px screenshots the plates, toy grid, job card, jug and cup, and the card all scale with the canvas; text stays inside the canvas; at most six large buttons show at once, and every drag also has a button route.

accessibility.evidence: axe WCAG 2.1 AA clean in both themes on desktop and phone in the walkthrough. All text on the canvas uses the theme text colour on tinted panels; the canvas aria-label reports what is on each plate, which toys you and Pip picked, the next job, how full the cup is and what the card says.
